notes.title: Thank you for an AMAZING Descenders Next Launch!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136442/698b71277a8237b4d25b0d703deb0e4786b3718b.png[/img]

Hi everyone!

It has been an incredible launch for Descenders Next! In just 24 hours, since we shadow dropped the game, we have had [b]over 100,000 of you[/b] jumping in and taking on the snowy peaks & dirt tracks! For context, it took the original Descenders 18 MONTHS to get those kind of numbers, so we are truly amazed at how many of you turned out to the launch, and we can't thank you enough!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136442/a5fb11339c6570c36991328f3f000f04a6b639f2.png[/img]

So, we've been receiving super useful feedback from you all while you've been playing, and we've already got a plan of things we're wanting to look at! Here is a quick run-down of a few things we've seen pop up often:
[list]
[*] [b]Speed:[/b] We know a lot of you are speed demons, but we hear that you'd like a bit more control over it too, so we're having a look at how we can make high speeds feel a bit easier to handle

[*] [b]Brakes:[/b] We've seen a few of you ask for some sort of brake mechanic to help with the high speeds, so this is something we're also taking a look at, which would also help with the speed topic from earlier

[*] [b]Multiplayer Game Modes:[/b] We hear you! We're looking at even more Multiplayer modes and opportunities to play with your friends, and more ways to smoothly progress through the map with your party
[/list]
We have so much more to come and so many cool things to add, be sure to check out the roadmap below to see some of the things we've got cooking! Be sure to join our [url=discord.gg/descenders]Discord[/url] too and chat with the community, and let us know your feedback there!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136442/6eaedc141d4c35022e8900c2f0ed1fadc1e01ee8.png[/img]

We want to thank you again so much for the helpful feedback & love you've given Descenders Next in the last 24 hours alone! We can't wait to see what the future holds!

- RageSquid & No More Robots <3

notes.title: 5 Years of Descenders!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

Can you believe it's been 5 years since the full launch of Descenders? And more since we put Descenders in Early Access? Neither can we! 

[h3][b]To celebrate, you can grab Descenders for 70% OFF as part of Steam's Replayability Fest!
[/b][/h3]

To keep the celebrations going, we thought we'd go over some pretty cool milestones over the last few years and recap all the cool stuff we've brought to Descenders, and the future of it too... 👀

[h2]Over 25 maps added since launch[/h2]

We haven't been shy in giving you new content since the launch of Descenders, adding over a whopping 25 maps, including some fan favourites such as Stoker, Jump City & more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30071847/f8f19f9252f8c493978e6570a55fcb3f669bf06f.jpg[/img]

notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/YV6yEge.jpg[/img]

[b]Hey everyone! [/b]

It's been a while since our previous update but we're here again with a big one! [i]New bikes, new physics, new tricks and so much more! [/i]

We've also asked the creators of some of the most popular mods on mod.io if we could integrate their maps directly into the game, this way we can bring them to non-Steam versions of Descenders as well. Next to porting these mods over we've also made 2 original bike parks. BikeOut4, the next installment in the BikeOut series, full of new and frustrating obstacles to have a go at. And New Lexico, the successor of Mt. Rosie, a massive open world with lots of areas to explore. 

[i]Console/PC Game Pass players: the content of this update will be heading your way very soon.[/i]

[b]New:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]New Bike parks.[/b]
Most are popular mods from mod.io integrated directly into the game (Aloda Lakes, Descenders Island, The Sanctuary, MegaPark, Kushmuck4x, Idarkopf). BikeOut 4 and New Lexico are two new and original maps made by us in collaboration with Spe (creator of Stoker Bike Park).
[*][b]New bike types.[/b]
The default Enduro bike can be changed to either a Hardtail or Downhill bike once you've obtained a sponsorship. You can change bike types in the Shed. 
[*][b]New bike physics.[/b]
Different bikes will have their own physics. While the hardtail is made for flippy bois with it's agile lightweight frame, the downhill bike is a sturdy, heavy and fast mean machine! 
[*][b]New tricks.[/b]
New tricks include the Tabletop, Superman Seatgrab, Barspin, Tailwhip and Tuck No Hander. Unfortunately to make room for these we had to say goodbye to the Candybar, we've built a memorial for it in Mt. Palumbo.
[*]30+ New customization items to unlock in career mode.

[*][b]Misc:[/b]
- Lots of sound effects added to BikeOut obstacles.
- Ambient sound added to all bike parks.
- Bowl Cam added to camera perspectives. Gives a better overview while playing in bowls and bike parks.
- Game client upgraded from x86 to x64. This should reduce the memory related crashes some people are experiencing.
[/list]

[b]Community[/b]
If you want to keep up to date with known issues and our current plans, join our [url=www.discord.gg/descenders]Discord[/url].

RageSquid & No More Robots

notes.title: Downhill biking game Descenders adds multiplayer as it exits Early Access
notes.notes:
Descenders is a downhill freeriding game where the worlds and trails are procedurally generated so you'll never quite know what to expect. It just left Early Access today and got a big feature update: Multiplayer. While you're challenging yourself with terrifying speeds down narrow, winding paths and hurtling through dizzying jumps upside-down, you'll now find yourself racing alongside other players.

I've been playing a bit today, working my way through the early stages of my downhill biking career and wiping out plenty of times along the way. The default keyboard controls take a bit of getting used to, but after a few courses they felt comfortable, and they can be fully remapped at any rate.

Wiping out isn't as funny as it is in, say, Trials, but it's still amusing. Especially when something happens like in the gif above, where it appears I've somehow gotten my torso wedged in my bike frame.

As you progress through your career, you'll also unlock bonus 'team members', who can influence the details of the next course by making the trail a bit wider or adding extra jumps or checkpoints. Descenders throws in randomly selected challenges in each course. If you complete the course without ever letting go of the acceleration key, for example, or by getting a total of six seconds of air, you'll gain an extra life which lets you crash one additional time on your next run.

Sometimes the map's features, difficulty, and challenges combine in interesting ways, such as when the map must be beaten in first-person mode, it's raining, and there's no actual trail, leaving you on a harrowing trip speeding between trees and rocks and desperately trying to spot the finish line. Make your way through the map and you'll reach the 'boss', a course with a massive jump. Beat a few boss jumps and you'll unlock new worlds to race through.

I haven't played a ton of it yet, but it's fun and exciting. Don't expect the procedural generation to be too bananas: This isn't No Man's Sky, after all, and plenty of courses have felt more or less the same even though there are small differences. It feels like just enough to throw a couple surprises in your path and keep you alert at all times. You can find Descenders on Steam, where it's 25% off for the next week.

notes.title: May 7 -- Descenders 1.0 -- The Multiplayer Update

[h1]It's here. Version 1.0. Multiplayer. May 7.[/h1]

After 15 months, and more than half a dozen major updates, Descenders is ready to leave Early Access. Thanks so much for taking this journey with us, and prepare yourselves for what the full Descenders experience has in store for you!

Here's what you can expect when The Multiplayer Update drops on May 7.

[h1]8 Player Online Multiplayer[/h1]

Imagine this: You boot up Descenders, into the brand new central hub (more on this below). All of a sudden, a bike goes flying by... then another... and another!

When you boot up Descenders, and anytime you go back to the main lobby, your hub will be filled with other players. You can ride around with them, check out high scores, explore the outskirts of the hub, whatever you like.

When you dash off into a Career session, you won't be alone either. You'll encounter random riders, playing the same seed as you in real-time. There are no collisions so you can't smash into each other, but you can race through the world and explore together.

[h1]Lobby Up With Friends[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/c3d7c8999d6e1da87d3780c96af38be5550087aa.gif[/img]

If you're not a fan of stranger danger, you can choose to start a Casual Lobby with friends. Invite your friends via Steam, and they can join up with you, and race through any of the worlds in the game.

It's up to you whether you race, explore, compete for score, mess around together, see if you can line up 7 riders and jump over all of them...

How you play Descenders with your friends is up to you!

[h1]Four Brand New Worlds[/h1]

Was five worlds not enough for you? How about four brand new worlds you've never played before?

Introducing CareerPlus Mode. When you've collected enough Rep, you'll unlock this mode which essentially gives you a whole new Career to play through, complete with four new worlds.

Check out the gifs for a sneak peek. And speaking of new areas...

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/814f482ecc776286ca740d2f1124da9f43c18be1.gif[/img]

Whenever you boot up the game or finish a run, you'll be booted into the new central hub area. It's much, much bigger than the original hub, and features a bunch of really cool areas to explore.

You can still find The Shed, and your team's tent, but you'll also find other useful areas, like a giant leaderboard that updates to show your best scores.

[h1]Loads of Other Stuff[/h1]

New music! New options! New sounds! New items! New bikes! New achievements! Play as a man or woman! New everything!

When the 1.0 Update hits on May 7, Descenders is going to feel like a very different game -- and we can't wait to share it with you.

See you all next week!

notes.title: Discord's version of Early Access now live, includes a few indie gems
notes.notes:
A month after launching its own game store, Discord's version of Early Access has gone live with an impressive five-game lineup.

The "first wave" of Discord Early Access games includes whimsical RPG Kynseed, cute dino management game Parkasaurus and downhill biking game Descenders, which could well be the heir to Skate's throne.

The other two games are Mad Machines, which is basically Rocket League with robots, and PT-inspired horror game Visage. Yes, it's only five games, but I'm impressed with the quality that Discord have pulled on board.

Mad Machines is the only one that's exclusive to Discord: it's part of the 'First on Discord' programme, which will see some games launch on the Discord store first as timed exclusives. The others are already part of Steam Early Access, and cost the same on Discord as they do on Steam.

One potential advantage over Steam, I suppose, is that playing through the Discord games launcher means you're already set up to chat to other members of the community and, sometimes, directly to the developers themselves by using Discord's verified servers. 

You can access the games through your Discord app or via its website, and you can find more details about the individual games on Discord's blog post.

notes.title: The Ring of Fire update is now live - 10% off!

Hey everyone!

It's time to turn up the heat! Introducing 'Volcano' as Descenders' new 5th environment! Getting there will be no easy task but once you're there it will take your breath away... or your health... that's up to you. Apart from the new environment we've made lots of other changes so let's get right to it.

[b]Important note for Xbox One players[/b]: This update also includes everything that was introduced in last month's Steam update, patch notes for this can be found [url=https://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791459593255/announcements/detail/1705057979404007707]here[/url]. This includes the teams rework, daily challenges, and a rework to the way bonus objectives are generated, among other good stuff. Check it out.

[b]Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Volcano:[/b]
- A new 5th environment, a completely different challenge, and unlocked by playing the game in a very specific way - the only hint we'll give is that it involves fiery rings of fire. ;)
- Volcano drops the 'stunts' parameter when generating a level and uses 'tectonics' instead. Hold on tight, this is gonna be a bumpy ride.
[*][b]New Bonus level:[/b]
- You've probably found the bonus levels we placed in highlands and peaks. This update introduces a MEGA interesting new one, see if you can find it.
[*][b]New Freeride options:[/b]
- People have been asking us to introduce the build crew to the freeride mode of Descenders, so that's what we did. 
- When setting up freeride parameters you can now go to a little menu with a dropdown list showing all of the build crew modifiers. [b]note[/b]: you need to have used each specific build crew member at least once in a regular session before you're able to use that one in freeride.
- We've split off the 'generate level from seed' and bonus levels and have given both their own place in the freeride menu.
- Bonus levels can now be played from the freeride menu, instead of having to enter it's level seed. [b]note[/b]: you need to complete a bonus level's objective before you unlock it for play in freeride.
[*][b]New unlocks:[/b]
- Added several new items of all rarities to unlock.
[*][b]Misc:[/b]
-Fire nodes are added to the world map, these are levels with their generation parameters maxed out to full intensity.

-Daily sponsor tasks now auto-claim after you've completed them.
-Daily sponsor tasks can be seen in the pause menu while in a session.
-Added 3 new achievements.
-Newsfeed now auto scrolls to next news story over time.
-Upgraded the item unlock screen so that it now shows you a 3D preview of what you've gotten.
-Greek translation added.
-A couple of new bike particles have been added.
-Pausing the game now fully pauses time as well.

-Bugfix (Xbox One): flow leaderboard fixed.

notes.title: Teams rework is here!
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/krqxxZZ.png[/img]

Hey everyone!

It's update time! We've overhauled the way teams/sponsorships worked, added a daily challenge mode, daily quests, and more! The road to sponsorship and the way you progress once sponsored has been changed. Therefore we've reset everyone's team. Your unlocks and Rep will not be taken away. It's a big one so let's get right into the changes.

[b]Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Teams rework:[/b]
- Obtaining a team no longer happens when reaching 1000 rep. Instead you'll have to complete 3 sponsor nodes on the world map instead before you get an offer.
- Sponsor nodes now give you a choice; you'll be able to start up an Arboreal, Enemy, or Kinetic track, regardless of which team you're in.
- Once sponsored you'll be able to complete daily sponsor tasks. These are refilled back up to 3 once per 24 hours. Completing sponsor tasks progresses you in your team, unlocking sponsor gear along the way.
- We've added the much requested option to leave your team! When leaving your team your sponsor progress will be reset to zero. Your Rep will not be reset, and your unlocks will not be taken away, but if you obtain a Kinetic sponsorship you won't be able to wear your Enemy gear, until you switch back to Enemy.
[*][b]Daily Challenge:[/b]
- In the Ride menu, you'll now find the Daily Challenge option. This starts up a regular session, except that you only get one chance per day. 
- The seed for this session is the same for all players and changes every day.
- Scores for the Daily Challenge are stored on a separate leaderboard and are viewable in the Standings menu.
[*][b]Bonus objectives rework:[/b]
- A common complaint was that bonus objectives often weren't doable on your current track. Our intention was that players could choose their next track based on the bonus objective they were given. In practice this didn't work very well so we shuffled some things around. The bonus objective will now be generated during track generation, it will randomly pick an objective from a pool of objectives that you're certainly able to complete on the current track.
[*]New bonus level. By now you've probably found the construction site in Highlands, can you find the new one as well? This one features a new type of objective as well.
[*]Session markers in freeride mode. Pressing 'T' or 'LeftStick' will plop down a marker in freeride levels, you can then respawn from there whenever you like.
[*]Mixer plugin updates. Should fix performance problems.
[*]Level generation build crew (all the yellow ones) are now included in level seeds. The old seeds will still work.
[*]Switched a few keybindings around on controller. Check the keybindings menu for new bindings for: toggle UI, skip song, and reset camera angle.
[*]Diminishing returns applied to stunts. Doing the same thing over and over will now award less Rep.
[*]Initial game loading sequence sped up.
[*]New team items added (by completing sponsor cards once sponsored).
[*]New generic unlocks added to the random item pool.
[*]Speedrun timer now in milliseconds.
[*]Stoppie nerfed, Fakie buffed, Stoppies & Wheelies now have diminishing returns applied.
[*]Construction site now has a separate finish line, so you are not forced to complete the objective.
[/list]

[b]Update platforms:[/b]
The update has been pushed live on Windows and Mac. Linux will be pushed live later today, or tomorrow at the latest. Xbox players will receive this update, combined with the next update, next month. This is due to the complicated and time costly nature of porting and updating on console.

[b]Community:[/b]
If you want to keep up to date with the known issues and our current plans, join our [url=www.discord.gg/descenders]Discord[/url], or have a look at the [url=trello.com/b/UIUrqPGq/descenders-roadmap]Roadmap[/url]! As always, we'd love to hear your thoughts!

Much love,
RageSquid & No More Robots

notes.title: The Rogue-Bike Update is here!
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/7hsF1z5.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone!

The Rogue-Bike update is here! We've revamped most of the existing systems (rep system, world map) and we're introducing a big new feature: the build crew. Let's dive into the changes right away:

[b]Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]World Map overhaul:[/b]
- Randomized start/finish line and level placement.
- Added more special nodes to the map. (Medic, First person, Danger zone, and more??)
- Day/night cycle. A new environment starts in the morning and playing a level advances the day. Reach the end of the world map before you run out of daylight.
[*][b]Rep system overhaul:[/b]
- Rep can no longer be lost. The risk of losing reputation made end-game players play very safe, this wasn't very fun to watch. In order to see more sick tricks we're introducing:
- Flow (rep per minute). Flow is the reputation one earns per minute, making sure that the players who are on top of the flow leaderboards are actually the most entertaining to watch as they constantly have to do the sickest stunts.
- New sessions start at 0 rep, the goal is to reach the end of the last environment with as much rep as possible. Session rep is added to your account rep after each session. Leaderboards will track 'best session rep', 'flow' (only on successfully completed runs), and 'overall account rep'.
- Diminishing returns. Doing the same trick over and over will reward fewer rep each time.
[*][b]Build crew:[/b]
- Build crew is a way to customize and tweak a session to the players liking.
- At certain rep milestones during a session new crew members will be unlocked. The player will have to choose one out of four randomly generated crew members (modifiers). Crew members last until the end of a session and a fresh session starts with 0 crew members.
- Crew members can be: wider paths when generating levels, higher bunny hops, decrease in off-road friction, generate fewer obstacles, always show the compass, and many others. Right now we've implemented 22 different build crew members and there are more to come! If you have ideas for other crew members, let us know!
[*]Removed the 'Practice' option when starting a new session. Practice session was a way to ride without consequences but after removing reputation losses this no longer feels needed.
[*]Removed dawn and night random visual modifiers. Storm can still randomly occur. Dusk now appears after having played 7 levels in the same environment. Night appears 2 levels after dusk. Completing a boss jump and entering a new environment resets the day timer.
[*]Mixer integration. Allows for interaction between viewers and streamers on the Mixer streaming platform.
[*]Speedrun timer. Enable in the gameplay settings to show a speedrun timer during your sessions. This timer ONLY pauses during loading screens.
[*]Added and tweaked a bunch of sound effects.
[*]Added a few new outfits, bikes, and accessories.
[*]Updated to a newer version of the Unity engine. This should improve the experience on lower end computers and macs.
[*]Performance upgrades across the board. We had to do a ton of performance upgrades when working on the Xbox version of Descenders. We took the ones that were applicable to PC/Mac/Linux and carried those over to the Steam version of Descenders.

notes.title: The Rogue-Bike Update: Coming May 15th
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/bace601ac7efa09b896d722a5aeb9d131ecb7c24.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone!

We're here today to give you some [b]pretty exciting news[/b].

A couple of months ago, the RageSquid team came up with a massive idea for Descenders that would make the game even more exciting and fulfilling, while fixing some of the issues people were having with the roguelike elements and the Rep system.

And now we're finally ready to unveil what we're calling [b]The Rogue-Bike Update[/b] -- and it's coming on [u]May 15th[/u].

Here's what you can expect:

[h1]The New World Map[/h1]

Currently, you play through the Career Mode world by world, and move from left to right on the world map. Other than picking what the new level will roughly contain in terms of steepness, stunts and curves, there isn't much to it. Until now.

With the Rogue-Bike Update, you'll now be tasked with exploring a randomized world map, filled with special nodes to discover. Your goal is still to reach the boss jump and clear it to move on to the next world, but you might want to ride around a little first and see what the world has to offer...

But don't ride around for *too* long. If you spend too much time exploring, the sun will begin to set, and you'll be plunged into darkness, making completing the boss jump a whole lot trickier.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/786e03a09f23cee5d42f9b9015dedd0f425d0e9d.png[/img]

[h1]The New Rep System[/h1]

The current Rep system is fine, but we've found that it stops the best players from wanting to take risks. All this will change with the Rogue-Bike Update.

From May 15th, each new run that you do will set your Session Rep back to zero, and you'll only earn Rep, rather than losing it. You'll also now be judged based on your Flow -- that is, your Rep per minute.

In other words, the better you ride and the more tricks you do, the better your Flow. And when you finish a Session, your Session Rep will be added to your Total Rep. Easy!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/28dd3d54c34c3f4ed83cd0040059e6558e315551.jpg[/img]

[h1]Crew Members[/h1]

Right now, once you've unlocked Canyon or Peaks, you might as well keep restarting from those worlds to reach the final boss. With the Rogue-Bike Update, we introduce Crew Members, who give you a reason to start from Highlands each time.

Every time you earn a certain amount of Rep on a run, you'll unlock a new Crew Member. These Crew Members will give you special mutators, such as softening all your landing impacts, or adding extra steepness or stunts to every level.

These mutators allow you to play the game your own way, and pick the abilities that matter to you. You can, of course, still start runs from later worlds, but you won't earn as many mutators that way.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30071847/5c7f08f217b55f796a96f4b78dba75546c4638a5.png[/img]

[h1]But what about my current Rep?[/h1]

On May 15th, we will reset all Rep scores. However, we will be giving special items to each and every Descenders player based on how much Rep they've earned before then:

[list]
    [*]If you've bought and played the game before May 15th, you'll earn a legacy item to show that you played before the Rogue-Bike Update
    [*]If you've earned more than 50,000 Rep by May 15th, you'll also earn an extra special legacy item
    [*]If you've earned more than 250,000 Rep by May 15th, you'll earn both of these items, and an extra, extra special legacy item
[/list]

[h1]When can I see the update in action?[/h1]

We'll be showing off the Rogue-Bike Update for the first time live on [url=http://mixer.com/nomorerobots]http://mixer.com/nomorerobots[/url] next Tuesday, May 8th, at 8am PT / 5pm CEST.

[b]EXCITING TIMES![/b]
Love Mike + RageSquid

We're back again with a small update! We've heard your feedback on the rep system and world map and we agree with you, they really need some work. notes.title: Downhill biking game Descenders could be the heir to Skate's throne
notes.notes:
For an indie developer in 2018, getting people to care about your game can be a daunting proposition, filled with all manner of marketing tactics and PR plans. But sometimes, all you really need to sell a game is a good gif.

That’s exactly how I discovered Descenders, the sophomore release from a tiny Dutch studio called RageSquid. For the last couple months, their Twitter feed has been an endless procession of gifs and short videos of a virtual mountain biker hurtling through a variety of pleasant environments at ludicrous speeds, jumping and flipping through the air.

With Descenders now hitting Early Access on Steam, I’m pleased to report that it mostly lives up to the excitement evoked by the footage that piqued my interest in the first place. While still light on content, the core experience is already enjoyable, and the dev team seems to have a solid plan for fleshing out the game going forward.

Right out of the gate, Descenders just plain feels good. It activates the same parts of my brain the old Skate games did, with a fairly simple system of analog inputs that can be fine tuned to infinity, or at least until I get that trick or jump just right. The bike handling is pleasantly responsive, if not terribly simulational, and the sound and art give the whole thing a satisfying solidity without going too overboard on state-of-the-art photorealism.

If you’ve been pining for a new game to play on the couch with friends, passing the controller back and forth every time you bail, this may be the game to finally scratch that eight-year itch that’s been left unscratched since the untimely demise of the Skate series. There’s also a laundry list of “gaps” in the Tony Hawk Pro Skater tradition, and a Spelunky-style “daily challenge” mode will be added shortly.

One of Descenders' main hooks is that all of its stages are procedurally generated, causing the terrain to change with every successive playthrough, but whether or not that’s a good thing isn’t quite clear yet. The nigh-infinite variety of courses is certainly nice, and for the most part Descenders does a good job of generating enjoyable routes, but occasional hiccups in the algorithm can be exceedingly frustrating in a game with as unforgiving of a progression system as this one.

You begin with four health, and can lose one to three points when you bail, depending on how hard you faceplant. Lose them all, and it's back to the very beginning of the world map. But thanks to the procedural levels, on several occasions I was presented with jumps that had such steep hills on the other side that hitting the jump caused me to pancake upon landing (and lose at least two of my precious four starting health), despite hitting the apparently 'correct' spot on the landing ramp. 

The bonus objectives, which while theoretically optional are the only way of restocking the health you lose upon crashing, are often rendered impossible by the vagaries of the terrain generation. An attempt to “do a 720” or “exceed 70km/h” can be foiled by a lack of large jumps, or a lack of sufficient steepness in the track, respectively. These issues can presumably be tuned out of the algorithm over time, but for the moment they remain rather frustrating.

Procedural generation issues aside, the primary reason I have a hard time wholeheartedly recommending Descenders in its current state is that there isn't all that much to it right now.

The roguelike-esque progression system is an interesting idea, but success won't reward you with new abilities to mess around with or statistical buffs. Descenders never really changes up the experience no matter how many runs you get through. There are cosmetic unlocks such as new bikes, shirts, and helmets, but those don’t change the play, and I felt like I’d more or less seen all there was to see after a couple hours of playing (though I could always just keep improving my skills, if I wanted).

Of course, that criticism comes with a major caveat: this is an Early Access game. More things to do are on their way, and the dev team has already announced a bunch of forthcoming features. Among these is the aforementioned daily challenge mode, as well as a tournament system, an expanded world map with new environments, and “rider improvements” (which may or may not mean real-deal, non-cosmetic unlocks).

I’m optimistic that Descenders will grow into a meatier game, and in the meantime, it’s a great way to kill a few hours in a super fun sandbox. I’m glad the developers chose to make something in such an under-populated genre, and devised a pretty unique format to boot. I expect Descenders' fate will largely be contingent on whether or not this fantastic core experience is fleshed out into something heftier.

notes.title: Descenders rides into early access on February 9th
notes.notes:
Downhill mountain biking sounds like a lark. What could be more pleasant than gliding down scenic valleys and weaving between the pines… at about 80kmh? Ah, yeah, I’d forgotten that bit. Downhill mountain biking sounds awful.

Google tells me that’s the top speed for real world bikers, but the ones in Descenders seem to eclipse that – as we’ll get to experience firsthand when the game launches on Steam Early Access February 9th. This isn’t RageSquid’s first foray into racing – they also made Action Henk, a game that’s sans bicycles but big on butt-sliding.

There’s more going on under the hood here (let’s just pretend that’s a thing bikes have) than in your typical racing game: the action takes place in procedurally generated worlds, which suggests you’ll have to think on your feet/wheels rather than practice the same bends again and again.

notes.title: The debut trailer for Descenders showcases risky downhill freeriding
notes.notes:
"The PC needs a new skateboarding game," we said back in May, and that remains the situation because, sorry to say, we're still not getting one. But we are getting something that might just scratch the sports on wheels itch: Descenders, an "extreme downhill freeriding" game that new indie publisher No More Robots described as "essentially Skate on bikes." 

Descenders makes use of procedurally generated maps and a "fully-fledged physics systems" that enables players to string together extreme combos on unique downhill runs. Make it to the bottom of the moutain without eating a tree, a rock, or other such unyielding bone-breakers, and you'll earn "Rep points" for you and your community-based team: Enemy, Arboreal, or Kinetic. Each has its own colors and gear, and they'll be in constant competition for top spot on the monthly leaderboards—and the prizes that come with it. 

Teams will also have leaderboards of their own, and members will have access to exclusive practice and social areas in the "Descenders Overworld." 

And it looks awfully fast. I haven't played it, like you I've only watched the trailer, but seeing the two-wheeled warrior get smoked by a hill, a ramp, and a tree made me wince a little on the inside. Always wear your helmet, kids. 

Descenders doesn't have a release date yet, but you can sign up for the upcoming beta by choosing your team at descendersgame.com.

notes.title: Descenders is a game about extremely brave bicycles
notes.notes:
Like most people, I don’t like falling down the stairs, so the prospect of falling down a hill or a mountain seems absolutely terrible. Incredibly, some people find falling very entertaining and they strap skis or boards to themselves expressly for the purpose of throwing themselves down slopes.

Descenders [official site] is the new game from the creators of butt-sliding action racing game Action Henk, and it’s all about falling down procedurally generated hills while attached to a bicycle. The announcement trailer, which you can see below, shows a bicycle jumping over a train and has a first-person section in which the bicycle is being attacked by trees. I might be scared of falling in real life, but I would happily fall down these digital hills.
